problems.title: Principal inverse trigonometric values
problems.question: Evaluate $\arcsin(-\sqrt3/2)+\arccos(\sqrt2/2)+\arctan\sqrt3+\operatorname{arccot}(-\sqrt3/3)$.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Use principal ranges: arcsin∈[−π/2,π/2], arccos and arccot∈[0,π], arctan∈(−π/2,π/2).
steps: The four values are−π/3,π/4,π/3,2π/3.
Their sum isπ/4+2π/3.

problems.title: Factor a trigonometric inequality
problems.question: Solve sin2x+2sinx>0.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
steps: The factor1+cosx is nonnegative and vanishes only when sinx=0 as well.
The strict inequality therefore holds exactly when sinx>0.

problems.title: Construct a cube section through three points
problems.question: In cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, M∈BB₁,N∈CC₁ and K is the center of ABCD. Construct the section through M,N,K, for MN∥BC and for MN meeting ray BC.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A section plane meets parallel face planes in parallel lines; two shared points determine each face trace.
steps: If MN∥BC, draw through K a line parallel to BC. It meets AB at U and CD at V. Join U to M on face ABB₁A₁ and V to N on face DCC₁D₁. Quadrilateral UMNV is the section.
If MN meets ray BC at T, extend MN to T. Since T is in both the section plane and base plane, draw TK. It meets AB and CD at U,V. Again join UM and NV; with MN and VU these bound the section.

The lines used lie in the corresponding faces, so all four edges are intersections with the same plane. For interior M,N these form a quadrilateral; endpoint cases follow by taking limits and merging coincident vertices.
problems.answer: The section is UMNV, constructed by the face traces described above.

problems.title: Prove a fourth-power cosine identity
problems.question: Prove 8cos⁴γ=3+4cos2γ+cos4γ.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
steps: 8cos⁴γ=2(1+2cos2γ+cos²2γ).
Substitute the second identity to obtain2+4cos2γ+1+cos4γ.
problems.answer: The identity holds for every real γ.

problems.title: A sine times an absolute cosine
problems.question: Solve sinx·|cosx|=√3/4.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The positive right side forces sinx>0. Squaring gives sin²x(1−sin²x)=3/16.
steps: Set u=sin²x. Then u²−u+3/16=0 gives u=1/4 or3/4.
In0<x<π this yields x=π/6,π/3,2π/3,5π/6. Each satisfies the unsquared equation.

problems.title: Inclination of a pyramid face
problems.question: In pyramid SABC, SC⊥ABC, ACB=90°, and SA,SB make45° and60° with the base. Find the tangent of the inclination of face SAB to the base.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Write SC=h. Then CA=h, CB=h/√3, and altitude from C to AB is CA·CB/AB=h/2.
steps: A perpendicular cross-section through SC and the foot on AB gives tanδ=SC/(distance C to AB).
Thus tanδ=h/(h/2).

problems.title: A rational inequality in cosine
problems.question: Solve cosx+(1+2cos2x)/(cosx−2)≥2sin²(x/2).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
steps: The inequality becomes (6c²−5c+1)/(c−2)≥0. The denominator is always negative.
Thus(3c−1)(2c−1)≤0, giving1/3≤cosx≤1/2.

problems.title: An inclined section of a square pyramid
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has base side10 and lateral edge5√5. Find the area of the section through a base edge inclined30° to the base.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
steps: Take the chosen edge at y=−5,z=0; the section plane is z=(y+5)/√3.
It meets the two opposite lateral edges at their midpoints, giving parallel section sides10 and5. Their projected separation is7.5.
The section’s actual height is7.5/cos30°=5√3. Area=(10+5)(5√3)/2.

problems.title: Exactly one trigonometric solution on an open interval
problems.question: Find a such that a cos²x+2(a+3)cosx+16=0 has exactly one root for π/2<x<π.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: On that interval c=cosx is one-to-one with−1<c<0. Solve a=−(6c+16)/(c²+2c).
steps: This parameter function is strictly increasing on(−1,0): its derivative is(6c²+32c+32)/(c²+2c)²>0 there.
Its limit at c→−1 is10 and at c→0 is+∞. Thus exactly one c exists for each a>10.

problems.title: Insphere and circumsphere of a regular triangular frustum
problems.question: A regular triangular frustum has a point distance3 from all five faces and a point distance R from all six vertices. The lower-base dihedral angle is60°. Find R.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The height is6 because the two parallel bases are tangent to a radius3 sphere. Let lower and upper base apothems be L,l.
steps: L−l=6cot60°=2√3. The sphere center is at mid-height; its distance to a lateral face gives (L−√3)sin60°=3, so L=3√3,l=√3.
Equilateral base circumradii are2L=6√3 and2l=2√3. Put the lower base at z=0 and upper at z=6.
The sphere center is on the axis at z=t. Equal squared vertex distances give108+t²=12+(6−t)², so t=−5.
